info.description: OEE component contract. The site-scoped /v1/sites/{site}/oee service (WIS-229) accepts calculations, seals candidate evidence and governs policies, with RFC 9457 errors. The legacy /v1/oee routes stay fail-closed (503). Callers authenticate with the OIDC browser session cookie; tenant and actor are never accepted from a payload. The WIS-270 evidence (/sources, /source-spans) and knowledge (entities, claims, reviews, conflicts, discovery inventories, freshness policy, process snapshots) routes are site-scoped with RFC 9457 errors; every mutation, creation included, takes Idempotency-Key, a quoted integer If-Match, X-CSRF-Token and a same-origin Origin, and answers 200. WIS-271 interview sessions persist participant-owned role interviews, deterministic discovery questions and append-only interview answer evidence. Site master data (WIS-520) provides revisioned lines, items, routings, shift calendars and site line-validation settings. All active site members can read; owner and supervisor roles can append revisions. Mutations require Idempotency-Key, quoted If-Match, X-CSRF-Token and same-origin Origin. Site configuration imports accept strict CSV for lines, items, shift calendars and routings, capped at 2,000 rows per file to keep the site lock within its 5-second writer lock timeout; raising this cap requires a faster import and a re-measured bound. Dry-run report digests bind the apply precondition to current site master data. OBJECT_ALREADY_CREATED identifies a deterministic import object ID that already exists with changed content and reports path ref. Configuration drafts (proposal F) hold candidate line, item, routing and workstation-profile revisions with field-level evidence citations; they are never live configuration. Owners and supervisors read and write drafts. Promotion appends the current draft revision through the normal revision path, requires every cited source to be available, and is refused (PROMOTER_IS_EDITOR) to the draft's author and every human editor. Promotion also requires a recent authentication. Idempotency-Key values starting with cfgdraft: are reserved for promotions and refused on direct revision routes. A request cites at most 500 field spans. Operational sources (WIS-270/272) are site-scoped and listed by source_id with a stable cursor. Every active member may read; registry and mapping writes require an owner or supervisor role with recent authentication. Batch intake uses its own event admission checks. A mapping revision takes If-Match on the mapping revision (X-Mapping-ETag) and appends a new source revision, which invalidates any earlier review approval. A row-level mapping problem carries path mappings[i].member with the caller's input index: 422 INVALID_SOURCE, 404 NOT_FOUND (unknown entity), 412 REVISION_CONFLICT (stale entity_revision) or 409 UNKNOWN_MAPPING (merged entity); a 412 without a path is a stale mapping revision. WIS-517 operations chat persists author-only, site-scoped conversations; a reply is data, never authority, and is an explicit non-answer until the answering loop is qualified. WIS-279 outcome feedback is append-only and site-scoped; the server binds the subject, case, context and evidence revisions, the reason is stored as data and never an instruction, and a correction overwrites nothing.

Statements are labelled approved_fact (a claim of the approved process snapshot the case context pins, in effect during the case's bound windows, with its validity interval and approved passages; a passage whose source is revoked leaves its fact out), observation (a server measurement of a bound window) or hypothesis (the stored, validated investigation output; one citation outside its run leaves every hypothesis out). post.description: Owner/supervisor only. CSRF required. Like profile-previews this computation persists no plan, approval, receipt or audit mutation, so no Idempotency-Key is required. Current order revisions and active master-data routing steps are resolved server-side. Optional item_id, routing_id and step_number link job orders and must be supplied together. item_code remains human display text. Catalog items have no code field, so unlinked codes cannot infer routing; link the job to a routing step. Knowledge snapshots are optional conflict cross-checks; missing or stale snapshots do not block. Limits: 50 orders, 200 operations, 100 stations, 100 merged downtime intervals; one concurrent solve per site. CP-SAT has a six-second deadline; unavailable, timed-out, invalid or infeasible solver output falls back to greedy. No placements returns 422 NO_FEASIBLE_SCHEDULE. The current plan format permits one job per station. Routing step order and selected knowledge precedence are enforced in the timing preview; cyclic or unplaceable dependencies carry reason codes. Operations outside the selection produce a warning. A dedicated session lock spans the solve, with no open database transaction during the child process.

200.description: Document verified and extracted (Word paragraphs and table rows, Excel sheets and rows, a born-digital PDF's pages one line per text row, CSV or text, values as stored). Its text and its automatic citable spans (consecutive lines, at most 2000 characters each) are created in one transaction as a document source; source.byte_length is the extracted size. The original bytes are not kept: original_sha256 identifies them and is bound by the Idempotency-Key, so a different file under the same key is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. A PDF is parsed in a short-lived, resource-capped child process. Refusals decided by the file are 4xx and resending it cannot succeed: 413 LIMIT_EXCEEDED over 20 MiB or when the text exceeds a source, PDF_TOO_MANY_PAGES over 1000 pages, PDF_PARSE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED when parsing needs more than its memory or time; 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA for executables, archives and a type that does not match the bytes, PDF_ACTIVE_CONTENT for JavaScript, attachments, launch, form submission or rich media, PDF_EXTERNAL_REFERENCE for hyperlinks and remote references (as DOCX external links); 422 UNREADABLE_SOURCE for macro-enabled, externally linked Office files, corrupt or textless files, PDF_ENCRYPTED, PDF_NO_TEXT_LAYER for a PDF without typed text (a scan, including one with an invisible OCR layer: read it by /source-scan-batches) or a page showing what neither its text nor the vision model can read (an annotation, an inline image, a form or pattern that shows anything, vector drawing on a page without typed text), PDF_TEXT_UNREADABLE for text that is not valid UTF-8, PDF_SCAN_HIDDEN_CONTENT for typed text the page hides from a reader (painted over or clipped, for example) or a figure the page does not show whole and plainly (off the page or its crop box, clipped, painted over, rotated, transparent, masked). A typed PDF's raster figures (at least 100 px on the shorter side and 2% of the page; smaller images are skipped and counted in images_skipped) are queued for the local vision model in the same transaction, one job per figure titled "<title> (page P, image K)" (image_reads); each becomes its own model-extracted source, designated only with confirm_model_extracted. At most 20 figures (413 PDF_TOO_MANY_IMAGES); 415 PDF_SCAN_IMAGE_UNSUPPORTED for a figure that is not JPEG or lossless; LIMIT_EXCEEDED for one over 4 MiB; 503 EXTRACTION_UNAVAILABLE for a PDF with figures when no vision model is configured. 503 EXTRACTION_BUSY (with Retry-After) when every parser slot is taken, and EXTRACTION_UNAVAILABLE when the parser cannot run: retrying the same key is safe. 503 SCAN_QUEUE_FULL (with Retry-After) when the figures would take the tenant past its cap on running scan pages (default 40); nothing is stored, and the same key retries

202.description: A scanned PDF (every page one JPEG, lossless or fax-encoded (CCITT Group 4 or one-dimensional Group 3, BlackIs1 false) image, no text layer, at most 20 pages; a fax page is decoded in the child to a PNG) screened like any PDF in a resource-capped child; each page's image is checked like a photo and queued for OCR, all pages in one transaction (page i keyed by a digest of the Idempotency-Key and i, so any valid key replays). A PDF with typed and scanned pages (WIS-645) also stores its typed pages as one typed document (never model-extracted) and links it with the page jobs as one upload (upload_id, document), all in one transaction; the same key replays it and another file under the key is 409. 422 PDF_SCAN_HAS_TEXT when no page is scanned (upload it to /source-documents), 415 PDF_SCAN_IMAGE_UNSUPPORTED for a JBIG2 or JPEG 2000 page, a fax page with other parameters (two-dimensional Group 3, BlackIs1, EndOfLine, columns or rows that are not its size) or a broken stream, a page with no or several images, 422 PDF_SCAN_HIDDEN_CONTENT for a page whose image is not shown whole and alone (a crop box, clip, mask, palette, annotation, drawing over it, placement off the page or on less than half of it, a page under one inch on a side, a page colour space, graphics state or group, or an image that is not a plain 8-bit grey, RGB or CMYK or 1-bit grey fax picture matching its dictionary: OCR reads the embedded image, so it could read what the page hides), 413 PDF_SCAN_TOO_MANY_PAGES, LIMIT_EXCEEDED for a page over 4 MiB or 40 megapixels (its declared size is checked before anything decodes it); other PDF refusals as for /source-documents. 503 EXTRACTION_UNAVAILABLE without a vision model. 503 SCAN_QUEUE_FULL (with Retry-After) when the pages would take the tenant past its cap on running scan pages (default 40, across all its sites): the batch is refused whole, nothing is stored, and a replay of a stored key is still answered.

The image is kept only while the job runs. 503 EXTRACTION_UNAVAILABLE when no vision model is configured. 503 SCAN_QUEUE_FULL (with Retry-After) when the page would take the tenant past its cap on running scan pages (default 40, across all its sites); nothing is stored, and a replay of a stored key is still answered.
